Overview

Microsoft partners are central to how Microsoft reaches and serves customers. The Partner Enablement organization, within Microsoft Business Operations, helps partners understand, prepare for, implement, and adopt changes across the partner lifecycle. 

The role independently leads complex, cross-functional partner enablement programs that bridge Microsoft strategy and partner execution. The Operations Key Account Manager develops a deep understanding of partner business models, capabilities, dependencies, and operational experiences; translates partner insight into clear recommendations and actionable business requirements; identifies and communicates risks early; and drives readiness and adoption for priority launches and change moments. Acting as a trusted advisor and Voice of Partner, this role is expected to create clarity in ambiguous situations, influence decisions without direct authority, and deliver measurable outcomes that reduce friction, strengthen trust, and improve the ease of doing business with Microsoft. 

 

Scope 

  • Operates independently on complex programs with broad cross-functional dependencies and material partner or business impact. 

  • Moves from analysis to a clear point of view, recommendation, and action plan; uses sound judgment to make progress when direction is incomplete. 

  • Leads through influence rather than formal authority, aligning stakeholders on outcomes, ownership, decisions, and timelines. 

  • Anticipates risks and dependencies, escalates with context and options, and drives issues to resolution with appropriate urgency. 

  • Communicates concise, decision-ready updates for leadership and adapts detail for partner, technical, operational, and executive audiences. 

  • Creates reusable approaches, operating rhythms, standards, and scalable solutions that improve outcomes beyond a single launch or partner. 

  • Leads the partner-facing change-management workstream from early impact assessment through sustained adoption, while keeping ownership of product, policy, platform, and technical delivery with the originating teams. 

  • Facilitates structured co-design among partners, engineering, product, business planning, operations, and launch teams to test assumptions, shape requirements, validate implementation feasibility, and resolve readiness risks before launch commitments are finalized. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond

 



Responsibilities

Partner Lifecycle Enablement and Trusted Advisory 

  • Drive partner enablement across end-to-end partner lifecycle processes to reduce friction and improve the ease of doing business with Microsoft. 

  • Build trusted relationships and structured engagement rhythms that surface partner priorities, operational pain points, requirements, risks, and emerging needs. 

  • Develop a practical understanding of partner business models, capabilities, technical and operational dependencies, and change impacts. 

  • Translate complex Microsoft business, product, engineering, policy, security, compliance, and platform changes into clear partner actions and operational implications. 

Voice of Partner and Advocacy 

  • Represent the Voice of Partner across Microsoft, using partner evidence and subject-matter expertise to influence requirements, design, prioritization, roadmaps, and launch decisions. 

  • Assess, clarify, and prioritize partner requirements, converting partner asks into actionable business requirements, recommendations, or experience improvements. 

  • Clearly articulate partner risks and concerns, including tangible business and operational impact, required ownership, and mitigation or risk-acceptance decisions. 

  • Connect individual partner experiences to broader patterns and systemic opportunities, and close the feedback loop with partners and internal stakeholders. 

Partner Co-Design and Engineering Collaboration 

  • Plan and facilitate co-design engagements with representative partners and engineering teams for changes that meet defined impact, complexity, or risk criteria. 

  • Frame clear co-design objectives, partner scenarios, decision questions, constraints, and expected outputs so sessions produce actionable evidence rather than general feedback. 

  • Translate partner workflows, technical dependencies, implementation effort, and operational constraints into prioritized requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, or design recommendations for engineering and business owners. 

  • Partner with engineering and product owners to identify what can be influenced, what is fixed, and what requires an explicit trade-off, exception, or risk-acceptance decision. 

  • Coordinate previews, pilots, sandbox or test-environment validation, and implementation walkthroughs to confirm that guidance, tooling, APIs, support paths, and operational processes are usable before broad release. 

  • Document decisions, owners, unresolved issues, and feedback disposition; close the loop with participating partners by explaining what changed, what did not, and why. 

Readiness, Adoption, and Change Management 

  • Own the partner change-management and readiness plan for priority launches and key change moments, including the change narrative, impacted partner segments, required partner actions, deliverables, milestones, dependencies, measures of success, risks, communications inputs, and stakeholder updates. 

  • Assess change impact and cumulative change burden across partner business models, geographies, roles, technical architectures, operational processes, and overlapping implementation timelines; identify where sequencing, scope, or support must change. 

  • Define readiness criteria and evidence for each change, distinguishing confirmed preparedness, at-risk status, not-ready status, and unknown status; use these signals to inform launch, mitigation, escalation, and exception decisions. 

  • Escalate blockers early with clear business impact, accountable ownership, and resolution needs; drive mitigation before critical milestones and go-live. 

  • Track implementation and adoption through and after go-live, confirm whether required partner actions and intended outcomes were achieved, and transition unresolved issues or sustained support needs to accountable owners. 

Data, Scale, and Continuous Improvement 

  • Use preparedness, adoption, operational, business, and qualitative data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and systemic gaps. 

  • Define measurable success criteria and deliver concise, decision-ready executive narratives that include a clear assessment, recommendation, trade-offs, and actions required. 

  • Apply a continuous-improvement mindset to standardize services, simplify processes, reduce manual work, and advance automation, AI-enabled insights, and self-service enablement models. 

  • Balance high-touch partner engagement with scalable and preventative solutions that address recurring friction across the broader ecosystem. 

Cross-Functional Leadership 

  • Demonstrate a One Microsoft approach by working seamlessly across engineering, business planning, product and launch, sales, operations, support, compliance, and enablement teams. 

  • Create clarity on accountability, decisions, and next steps; independently convene and align the right stakeholders to solve ambiguous, cross-organizational problems. 

  • Influence without direct authority using partner evidence, sound judgment, business impact, and data; confidently recommend a path forward when information is incomplete. 

  • Demonstrate thought leadership, strategic thinking, adaptability, and proactive identification of end-to-end opportunities that drive business impact. 

Success in This Role 

  • Partners understand the change, know what actions are required, and are prepared to implement and adopt it with greater confidence and less friction. 

  • Partner requirements and risks are surfaced early enough to influence design, launch, process, policy, or operational decisions. 

  • Readiness plans provide an honest, timely view of progress, dependencies, blockers, ownership, and decisions required. 

  • Partner insights are translated into measurable improvements and scalable solutions rather than repeated one-off interventions. 

  • Cross-functional teams have clear accountability and shared understanding of partner impact, priorities, and outcomes. 

  • Representative partners and engineers have validated critical scenarios, requirements, technical guidance, and implementation paths early enough to influence the solution or make explicit risk decisions. 

  • Readiness status is evidence-based, distinguishes known risk from unknown status, and drives timely decisions on sequencing, mitigation, exceptions, and launch confidence. 

  • Change-management plans address partner awareness, understanding, capability, implementation, adoption, reinforcement, and closed-loop learning rather than stopping at communications or launch completion. 

  • Embody our culture and values


Qualifications

Minimum / Required Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 4+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement OR equivalent experience.

 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, Technology, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field AND 8+ years of relevant experience, OR equivalent experience. 

  • Experience working in global, cross-functional, and highly matrixed environments. 

  • Proven record of delivering complex programs, launches, operational changes, or improvement initiatives with competing priorities. 

  • Demonstrated experience in partner channel management, partner operations, customer relationship management, customer success, or strategic account engagement. 

  • Ability to translate technical, operational, and business requirements into clear plans, recommendations, and executive-ready communications. 

  • Strong project and change-management capability, including change-impact assessment, stakeholder and resistance planning, readiness criteria, adoption measurement, navigating ambiguity, resolving conflict, negotiating trade-offs, and developing practical solutions. 

  • Strong analytical capability using data, reporting, dashboards, KPIs, and qualitative insight to influence decisions and monitor outcomes. 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex subjects to global audiences and engage effectively across levels and cultures. 

  • Demonstrated impact and influence skills, including cross-boundary collaboration and relationship building with internal and external stakeholders. 

  • Experience identifying systemic issues and applying industry practices, standardization, automation, AI, continuous improvement, or self-service solutions to improve scale and sustainability. 

  • Understanding of cloud, commerce, digital platforms, partner ecosystems, security, compliance, or lifecycle operations is advantageous. 

  • Independent, flexible, proactive, and able to identify strategic opportunities, develop proposals, and gain stakeholder alignment. 

Core Capabilities 

Partner Advocacy and Voice of Partner | Partner Co-Design and Engineering Collaboration | Strategic Business Analysis | Program and Change Management | Readiness and Adoption | Data-Informed Decision Making | Risk Management | Executive Communication | Cross-Functional Influence | Relationship Management | Continuous Improvement | Automation and Scale

Join Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I), the organization behind the technology and infrastructure that powers Microsoft’s cloud. Within CO+I, the Trusted Cyber Engineering (TCE) team is at the forefront of ensuring the security of our global operations.

 

We are seeking a highly skilled security engineer to join our team dedicated to driving cutting-edge security innovation. You will test physical and logical security systems that keep Microsoft’s global datacenter running, from cloud services and networks to hardware and operational technology for critical infrastructure such as power, cooling, and building management systems. As part of our team, you’ll provide guidance on team priorities, tactics, and methodologies. You will educate, empower, and inspire fellow cyber defenders, peers, and strategic partners. Our focus is collaboration as we perform penetration testing and ensure a high rate of issue resolution working very closely with our partners. You will be a direct hands-on individual contributor and a technical lead for our penetration testing function with the ability to help shape the team and team’s strategy as we continue to mature our penetration testing team’s capability and growth.

 

While there is a preference for candidates who can work from our Redmond, WA office three days per week, we welcome qualified candidates who may not be able to meet this preference.

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals.   • Leads and participates in comprehensive penetration testing efforts across all layers of services including applications, cloud, network, hardware and critical infrastructure operational technology (OT) systems. Identifies security vulnerabilities, performs end-to-end adversary emulation within approved rules of engagement for multiple areas of responsibility with an ability to come up to speed on new targets and unidentified patterns without direction.
  • Operates in uncertain, challenging, and novel environments and execute offensive and defensive security operations. Identifies unknown risk areas and leverages expertise to appropriately handle them. 
  • Builds relationships to enable streamlined and efficient communication and collaboration, advocating for security change across the organization.
  • Provides strategic guidance to teams on priorities, tactics, evaluation strategies, and development of methodologies. Chains findings into attack paths that demonstrate operational and business impact.
  • Organizes and directs the team focused on engagement rules, scoping, executive risk communications and technical guidance for operations. Leads the rhythm of business across team to ensure remediation of findings is completed according to the defined SLA; reporting and all communications are delivered on time.
  • Creates high-quality executive level verbal and written presentations advocating for and outlining process of penetration testing, explaining technical information to non-technical audiences, as well as present data driven reporting tracking operations, explaining impact, risks, vulnerabilities, system information and remediation plans with potential impact.
  • Works as a technical operator on various types of penetration testing offerings with an ability to identify and exploit misconfigurations, improve detection capabilities, and enhance threat visibility.
  • Research emerging threats, vulnerabilities, and tools to stay updated with the latest attack techniques, and security trends
  • Mentors and guide team members and partners, fostering a culture of curiosity, collaboration, and technical excellence. Partners closely with detection, threat intelligence and incident response teams to turn findings into actionable detections.
  • Applies AI and automation to scale reconnaissance, discovery and testing.

The Commerce organization builds and operates scalable, resilient, and AI-powered data platforms that transform complex financial and infrastructure data into trusted insights, enabling faster, data-driven business decisions. We are hiring a Principal Software Engineer to architect, design and develop a large-scale data platform that delivers actionable insights into data center infrastructure capacity utilization and product consumption revenue and enable business teams with key insights.

 

This role sits at the intersection of cloud-native distributed systems, advanced data engineering, and AI-powered software engineering. The successful candidate will define the technical vision and architect large-scale data platforms that transform massive volumes of infrastructure telemetry, consumption, and revenue data into trusted, explainable insights that drive capacity planning, infrastructure optimization, operational efficiency, and CapEx investment decisions.

 

As a technical leader, you will own the architecture of data ingestion, processing and modeling analytics. You will leverage AI-assisted development and agentic engineering workflows to accelerate software delivery, modernize complex data systems, and establish engineering practices that enhance developer productivity, system reliability, and analytical accuracy. The ideal candidate combines deep hands-on engineering expertise, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to navigate ambiguity and influence cross-organizational initiatives while delivering measurable business impact at scale.

 

This role requires you to be onsite 3 days a week in Microsoft’s offices in Redmond, WA.

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

 

  • Architect highly scalable distributed data systems to process massive volumes of infrastructure telemetry, and cloud product consumption data.
  • Design reusable data processing frameworks, canonical data models, and data contracts that accommodate evolving business requirements.
  • Establish robust data engineering patterns for incremental processing, late-arriving data, historical backfills, reconciliation, lineage, and schema evolution.
  • Lead architectural decisions across cloud data platforms, distributed compute engines, data lakes, streaming and batch processing, and analytical serving systems, balancing data freshness, correctness, performance, and cost.
  • Deliver actionable, explainable insights using AI and advanced analytics to drive business impact and data-driven decision-making.
  • Design AI-powered software engineering workflows leveraging coding agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), domain knowledge repositories, and tool-integrated agents to accelerate development and modernization of large-scale data systems.
  • Apply AI to analyze legacy codebases, map dependencies, generate implementation plans, automate refactoring, and improve test generation and code quality.
  • Develop agentic workflows to streamline data pipeline development, code reviews, failure triage, root-cause analysis, and operational knowledge discovery.
  • Establish governance and quality guardrails for AI-generated code, including automated testing, data correctness validation, security reviews, and production-readiness checks.
  • Drive measurable improvements in engineering productivity, development lead time, test automation, defect reduction, pipeline reliability, observability, and recovery time
  • Embody our culture and values. 


Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 6+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to Scala, Python, C#, Java OR equivalent experience.

Preferred/Additional Qualifications:

  • Expertise in architecting, building, and operating production-grade, cloud-native data platforms using Microsoft Fabric, Azure Synapse, Azure AI Foundry, Azure Machine Learning, or equivalent technologies.
  • Deep proficiency in Apache Spark, Delta Lake, distributed systems, SQL, or large-scale batch and streaming data processing.
  • Demonstrated programming skills in Scala, Python, C#, Java, or equivalent, with a focus on maintainable, testable, and high-performance production software.
  • Extensive experience in data modeling, analytical data systems, and SQL-based data analysis, including translating ambiguous business requirements into actionable metrics and insights.
  • Proven ability to optimize distributed workloads, compute, storage, query execution, data partitioning, and processing costs.
  • Experience building reliable data platforms with robust data quality, observability, governance, lineage, and operational excellence.
  • Demonstrated understanding of statistical analysis, time-series analytics, anomaly detection, and forecasting.
  • Practical experience applying AI coding assistants, LLMs (Large Language Models), and agentic workflows to software development, code modernization, testing, and engineering automation.
  • Understanding of RAG (retrieval-augmented generation), embeddings, semantic search, tool calling, and agent orchestration, with experience implementing appropriate security, correctness, reliability, and human oversight controls.
  • Proven ability to lead cross-team technical initiatives, influence architecture and engineering strategy, navigate ambiguity, and deliver measurable business outcomes.

Overview

As AI reshapes how organizations create, share, and consume information, the ability to protect sensitive data and prevent its unintended exposure has emerged as one of the most critical challenges facing every enterprise.

At Microsoft, we are committed to helping organizations secure AI to enable trustworthy AI transformation. This role sits at the center of that transformation, helping organizations build the trusted data foundation required to adopt AI securely, protect their most valuable assets, and enable innovation with confidence at scale.

Microsoft Security is looking for a Product Marketing Manager to join the Secure Data Solution Marketing team and lead marketing efforts for our practitioner audience, including driving usage of Purview, our data security product. This role will connect the dots across the lower funnel, using customer and product signals to identify where users encounter friction, uncover the pathways that lead to successful adoption, and translate those insights into experiences that drive sustained usage.

You will work across scale channels including trials, product-led growth (PLG), relationship marketing, in-product experiences, documentation, Tech Community, and practitioner engagement. You’ll partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Marketing teams to identify high-impact usage opportunities, test new approaches, and build repeatable motions that help customers realize value faster.

 We’re looking for a customer-obsessed marketer to join our team of collaborative marketing members who are individually brilliant, love working with each other, take ownership, and embrace a growth mindset. The ideal candidate has deep customer empathy and is technically credible, with the ability to turn real customer challenges, deep product understanding into clear strategy and high-quality content. They are both strategic and hands-on, and build trusted partnerships across product, engineering, sales, marketing, and leadership teams to drive alignment and results.



Responsibilities
  • Drive usage across the customer journey. Identify opportunities to move customers from trial and initial engagement to deeper, sustained product usage across scale channels.
  • Uncover the paths to adoption. Analyze customer behaviors and usage signals to identify friction, drop-off points, and the “golden paths” that correlate with successful adoption.
  • Connect insights across channels. Bring together signals from trials, PLG, relationship marketing, Tech Community, practitioner engagement, and other customer touchpoints to develop an integrated view of the customer journey.
  • Turn insights into experiences. Translate customer and product insights into targeted experiences such as lifecycle email, in-product prompts, documentation, videos, technical content, webinars, and Tech Community AMAs. Test, learn, and optimize. Develop hypotheses, execute experiments, measure results, and continuously improve experiences based on customer behavior and performance data.
  • Build repeatable usage motions. Codify successful experiments into scalable programs and playbooks.
  • Champion the practitioner. Develop a strong understanding of data security practitioners, their workflows, and the barriers that prevent them from realizing product value.

  • Master's Degree in Marketing, Computer Science, Business or related field AND 3+ years experience in business OR Bachelor's Degree in in Marketing, Computer Science, Business or related field AND 5+ years experience in business OR equivalent experience.
  • Experience developing and executing customer adoption, engagement, lifecycle, or product-led growth programs.
  • Experience using quantitative and qualitative customer insights to identify opportunities and translate them into actionable marketing programs. Demonstrated ability to manage cross-functional projects and execute programs across multiple teams and stakeholders. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts and customer insights into clear, compelling experiences.

SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Teams, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for engineers to help achieve that mission. 

The Compute Silicon & Manufacturing Engineering (CSME) organization within SCHIE is responsible for design, development, manufacturing and packaging of Microsoft's state-of-the-art computer chips, notably the Azure Cobalt. Our solutions provide sustainable strategic advantages to Microsoft and enable our customers to achieve more. 

As Microsoft's cloud business continues to grow the ability to deploy new offerings and hardware infrastructure on time, in high volume with high quality and lowest cost is of paramount importance. To achieve this goal, the Verification & Validation team is instrumental in defining and delivering operational measures of success for hardware manufacturing, improving the planning process, quality, delivery, scale and sustainability related to Microsoft cloud hardware. We are looking for experienced engineers with a dedicated passion for customer focused solutions, insight and industry knowledge to envision and implement future technical solutions that will manage and optimize the Cloud infrastructure.

 We are looking for a Senior Design Verification Engineer – Fabric Interconnect to join the team.

 

#SCHIE #CSME



Responsibilities

The candidate for this position will be expected and able to complete the following responsibilities:

  • Own or lead aspects of integration-level verification of Fabric Top, spanning coherency (e.g., CHI), PCIe/CXL traffic, and configuration access traffic
  • Learn about the design and interact with partner IP and SOC teams as well as VIP teams to define verification strategies and test plans
  • Develop UVM/System Verilog based verification environments at the integration level, and run and debug simulations to drive quality
  • Leverage Automation, Formal-based methods, and AI based approaches as an additional tool in the verification toolkit
  • Innovate to improve verification efficiency through methodologies or tools
  • Apply industry leading generative AI solutions to verification work
  • Coach and mentor others in your areas of expertise
  • Demonstrate Microsoft core values: Customer Focus, Adaptability, Collaboration, Growth Mindset, Drive for Results, Influence for Impact, Judgement, and Diversity & Inclusion

  • Demonstrated expertise in leading verification of designs that utilize Coherent Hub Interface (CHI) and Advanced Microcontroller Bus Architecture (AMBA) protocols
  • Demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following: fabric interconnects, coherency, virtualization, security, interrupts, PCIe, CXL, and/or protocol bridges

Apple’s wireless chip powers connectivity across every new iPhone — and its successor is already taking shape. Would you like to join Apple’s growing wireless silicon development team? Our wireless SOC organization owns every aspect of wireless silicon development, with a particular emphasis on highly energy-efficient design and new technologies that transform the user experience at the product level. It is driven by a world-class, vertically integrated team spanning RF/Analog, Systems/PHY/MAC, VLSI/RTL design and integration, Emulation, Design Verification, Test and Validation, and FW/SW engineering. As a Wireless SOC Design Verification Engineer, you’ll be at the heart of the chip design effort — owning a meaningful verification scope and growing it project to project.

Description

You’ll be responsible for pre-silicon RTL verification at the block, subsystem, and top-level SOC, taking your scope from test planning through coverage closure and signoff. Working closely with architects, designers, and firmware engineers, you’ll build reusable testbenches and verification environments using modern, metric-driven methodology. Areas you may work on include the Power Management Unit, CPU subsystem, DMA, on-chip debug infrastructure, PCIe, bus fabric, boot and secure-boot sequencing, MAC-PHY Verification, Radio integration, and peripherals such as SPI — choosing simulation, formal, or whichever approach the design actually calls for. Low power is part of your scope wherever it shows up: you’ll verify power intent using UPF within your area.

Over time, you can grow deeper into the IPs and subsystems you know best, or broader — across IPs and up from block level to full SOC integration. The team is also pushing hard on AI-assisted verification, and you’ll help figure out where it fits best: test generation, debug, coverage closure, or all the above.

Responsibilities

Partner with architects and designers early to build detailed verification plans from specifications — before RTL lands, not after.
Develop reusable block/IP and subsystem-level UVM testbenches, and support IP integration into the SOC.
Write directed and constrained-random tests; create and analyze coverage models and drive coverage closure.
Debug failures, including corner cases, and manage bug tracking through resolution.
Verify low-power design intent using UPF within your scope.
Verify end-to-end WiFi and Bluetooth traffic flows from subsystem level up through top-level SOC integration.
Apply formal verification where it fits — the team will help you ramp up.
Build and improve automated regression flows and contribute to methodology in your area.
Explore and apply AI-assisted verification techniques to improve team productivity.
Participate in verification reviews and uphold high coding-quality standards.
Support post-silicon bring-up as needed.

Minimum Qualifications

BS and a minimum of 10 years relevant industry experience.
Hands-on experience across the verification cycle: test planning, testbench implementation, test creation and debug, and coverage closure.
Strong SystemVerilog and Verilog skills, with solid working knowledge of UVM.
Solid problem-solving and debugging skills with constrained-random verification.
Understanding of digital logic design, SOC architecture, and microarchitecture.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience taking at least one ASIC/SOC from concept through tape-out.
Verification experience with PCIe, bus fabric/NOC, or AHB/AXI-based architectures in a UVM environment.
Experience verifying IP or top-level integration for a WiFi or Bluetooth SOC, or knowledge of wireless protocols.
Experience with low-power verification, UPF, boot-up, power-cycling, and HW/FW interaction.
Experience with SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) and/or formal tools (e.g., JasperGold).
Experience defining coverage space and writing coverage models.
Experience with embedded CPU verification; programming in C/C++ or assembly.
Scripting in Python or Perl; interest in applying AI/ML to verification workflows
Great teammate with excellent communication skills and the desire to take on diverse challenges.

Low power is part of your scope wherever it shows up: you’ll verify power intent using UPF within your area.

Over time, you can grow deeper into the IPs and subsystems you know best, or broader — across IPs and up from block level to full SOC integration. The team is also pushing hard on AI-assisted verification, and you’ll help figure out where it fits best: test generation, debug, coverage closure, or all the above.

Responsibilities

Partner with architects and designers early to build detailed verification plans from specifications — before RTL lands, not after.
Develop reusable block/IP and subsystem-level UVM testbenches, and support IP integration into the SOC.
Write directed and constrained-random tests; create and analyze coverage models and drive coverage closure.
Debug failures, including corner cases, and manage bug tracking through resolution.
Verify low-power design intent using UPF within your scope.
Verify end-to-end WiFi and Bluetooth traffic flows from subsystem level up through top-level SOC integration.
Apply formal verification where it fits — the team will help you ramp up.
Build and improve automated regression flows and contribute to methodology in your area.
Explore and apply AI-assisted verification techniques to improve team productivity.
Participate in verification reviews and uphold high coding-quality standards.
Support post-silicon bring-up as needed.

Minimum requirement of a bachelors degree.

Strong SystemVerilog and Verilog skills, with solid working knowledge of UVM.
Solid problem-solving and debugging skills with constrained-random verification.
Understanding of digital logic design, SOC architecture, and microarchitecture.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience taking at least one ASIC/SOC from concept through tape-out.
Verification experience with PCIe, bus fabric/NOC, or AHB/AXI-based architectures in a UVM environment.
Experience verifying IP or top-level integration for a WiFi or Bluetooth SOC, or knowledge of wireless protocols.

The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds the container and virtualization runtime technology that powers Apple's next-generation compute platform. We're a fast-moving, highly skilled team of systems engineers designing and developing the virtualization-based runtimes that run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center and Apple platforms — with privacy, security, and performance as first-class requirements. Beyond the datacenter, we maintain Apple Container, our open source project bringing native container support to macOS desktops.

We're looking to add talented, passionate seasoned domain experts who love hard systems problems and want to build foundational technology used across Apple and the open source community, ready to take ownership of significant technologies.

Description

We build the container runtime technology that Apple's own services and developers depend on. Our systems engineers develop virtualization-based runtimes — using macOS virtualization and VMM solutions like Cloud Hypervisor and sandboxed container solutions — to run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center and Apple platforms, with a relentless focus on privacy, security, and performance. This is a foundational systems team: we work at the level of kernel and container security, image distribution, filesystems, and virtualization. Much of this work is greenfield, solving problems unique to running on Apple's own hardware in the data center, at a scale and with constraints the rest of the industry hasn't had to solve for. Beyond the datacenter, we maintain Apple Container, our open source desktop tooling that lets developers around the world run containers natively on macOS.

We're looking for a domain expert with depth across multiple technical areas, someone used to designing major features and resolving highly complex, ambiguous problems creatively — taking ownership of significant technologies to drive real impact across the organization, ready to take risks, course-correct quickly, and drive ideas from inception to implementation, building a reputation as someone the broader org seeks out for technical direction and standards, and to actively mentor engineers at all levels.

We love open source and collaboration at every level.

Come join Apple's growing wireless silicon development team. Our wireless SoC organization is responsible for all aspects of wireless silicon development, with a particular emphasis on highly energy-efficient design and new technologies that transform the user experience at the product level. All of this is driven by a world-class vertically integrated engineering team spanning RF/Analog architecture and design, Systems/PHY/MAC architecture and design, VLSI/RTL design and integration, Emulation, Design Verification, Test and Validation, and FW/SW engineering. In this role, you will help de-risk our silicon well ahead of tape-out by owning the pre-silicon emulation environment that enables the team to exercise and verify new designs early and with confidence. We are looking for a wireless PHY systems engineer for this role: your understanding of the full signal chain, from RF and PHY through MAC and firmware, will help ensure that each emulated design not only comes up but behaves as intended. Prior Palladium experience is not required, and we will help the right candidate ramp up on the platform. If you enjoy a fast-paced and challenging environment, collaborate with people across different functional areas, and thrive during crisis times, we encourage you to apply.

Description

This role is central to Apple's pre-silicon verification effort for wireless SoCs, centered on the Palladium emulation platform. You will be the first to bring up each newly released emulation build, and you will design and own the framework and infrastructure — register maps, initialization and boot sequences, clock and reset, and system-level configuration — that brings the emulated SoC into an operational state and enables the wider team to run their own design verification. Working at the intersection of digital design, firmware, and validation, you will own and evolve this infrastructure across successive silicon generations, while also contributing to pre-silicon emulation and lab bring-up of Bluetooth and UWB silicon.

Responsibilities

Act as the initial validation point for each released Palladium emulation build, performing early smoke and sanity testing to confirm the build is functional, correctly configured, and ready for broader team use.
Build and own the framework and infrastructure that exercises the Palladium build — including register map definitions, initialization and boot sequences, clock and reset setup, and other system-level configuration — to bring the emulated SoC into an operational state.
Abstract platform bring-up and configuration complexity into reusable infrastructure and tooling, enabling the rest of the team to concentrate on their own design verification rather than platform-level setup.
Sustain, extend, and maintain this emulation infrastructure across multiple silicon generations, establishing it as a long-lived, reusable platform rather than a per-project effort.
Support pre-silicon emulation efforts for silicon validation, including test development, debug, and performance characterization on emulation platforms.
Bring up, test, characterize, and optimize Bluetooth and UWB silicon in the lab, ensuring robust performance across real-world operating conditions.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree with 10 years of relevant experience.
Solid foundation in Digital Signal Processing (DSP) and wireless communications, with working knowledge of PHY and MAC layer concepts.
Hands-on software programming skills for system modeling, simulation, and test, with proficiency in MATLAB and C/C++.
Familiarity with analog/RF impairments common in wireless systems (e.g., phase noise, IQ imbalance, nonlinearity).
Experience with or knowledge of wireless standards such as Bluetooth, Ultra-Wideband (UWB), or other wireless protocols.
Experience collecting, processing, and visualizing large-scale simulation and test datasets, including performance metrics such as measurement accuracy, latency, and throughput.
Strong communication skills, both written and oral, with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree with 10 years of relevant experience.
Hands-on experience in wireless chip or modem development, with a strong systems-level understanding of cross-layer dependencies between RF, PHY, MAC, and firmware.
Hands-on experience in Bluetooth and UWB systems design and validation.
Digital design fundamentals and a solid understanding of SoC architecture and system-level hardware/software interaction.
Hands-on RTL experience (Verilog/VHDL) and experience with register map and programming-model definition.
Experience with fixed-point design, RTL vector generation, and/or High-Level Synthesis (HLS).
Experience with pre-silicon emulation (e.g., Palladium) or FPGA prototyping, including build bring-up, debug, and performance characterization.
Experience developing validation frameworks and infrastructure, including initialization sequences, clock and reset setup, and system-level configuration.
Experience in lab FPGA/silicon bring-up, PHY/RF/MAC testing, and use of RF lab equipment.
Proficiency with Python for test automation and data analysis, and experience with simulation automation, regression frameworks, or CI/CD pipelines.
Experience collaborating with firmware and FPGA/emulation engineers to bring up, integrate, and debug hardware platforms, ensuring correct hardware/software interaction.

Meta's Edge & Network Services team is responsible for the deployment and operational support of production networks spanning Edge, Backbone, Optical, and Datacenter infrastructure across Meta's global footprint. You will partner with cross-functional teams to execute network deployments, drive operational excellence, and contribute to the evolution of global network standards.

Responsibilities

  • Deploy, configure, and validate production network infrastructure including switching, routing, and optical transport equipment across data center and edge sites
  • Perform day-to-day operational support of site network services, including troubleshooting routing and switching protocol issues across BGP, IS-IS, MPLS, and RSVP-TE environments
  • Plan and execute scheduled maintenance activities including hardware upgrades, software migrations, and decommissioning of production network assets
  • Maintain accurate as-built documentation, asset inventory, and configuration records for all deployed network and physical infrastructure
  • Collaborate with network design and architecture teams to implement scalable deployment standards and contribute to the development of new site service solutions
  • Support integration and field testing of new hardware and software platforms prior to production rollout
  • Partner with vendors and facilities teams to manage structured cabling, fiber-optic infrastructure, and physical layer dependencies at production sites
  • Participate in an on-call rotation to provide 24x7 support for production network infrastructure and respond to network incidents
  • Identify opportunities to leverage automation and AI-assisted tooling to streamline deployment workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve operational consistency
  • Contribute to team-level goals by sharing operational learnings, documenting best practices, and advising cross-functional partners on complex network matters

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience with physical network infrastructure including structured cabling, fiber-optic cabling, and data center facility operations
  • Experience working in multi-vendor network environments with hands-on exposure to enterprise or hyperscale networking hardware
  • Experience with network protocols including TCP/UDP, DHCP, and DNS, and hands-on experience with both IPv4 and IPv6 environments

We are looking for a Forensic Technologist to join our eDiscovery and Information Governance Legal Team. In your role as a Forensic Technology Lead, you will focus on discovery/disclosure efforts in the various phases of the EDRM model for litigation and regulatory matters, investigations, and all other matters requiring the identification, preservation, collection, processing, and production of data. This is a full-time role located in either our New York, NY or Washington, DC office location. You will collaborate with a variety of technical and non-technical stakeholders, including case managers, project managers, information governance specialists, data scientists, and attorneys, as well as outside vendors. You will provide overall guidance and recommend best practices for extracting, processing, and filtering data in a defensible manner. You will be responsible for delivering technology related client services in the areas of data mapping and documentation, forensic data collections, data extraction, data processing, data review, as well as digital and forensic extraction and analysis. You will be responsible for having deep knowledge of the SAAS collection and processing tools utilized by the team as well as evaluating alternative tools in the marketplace. You should also have a working knowledge of the laws that govern discovery and should be prepared to testify on the Company’s behalf relating to the defensibility of our processes during discovery disputes.

Responsibilities

  • Collect and analyze data from a variety of electronic media and company data sources, including ability to perform imaging of computers, laptops, cell phones, tablets and other devices, and ability to collect from a variety of cloud-based repositories, internal tools, collaboration tools and company data sources
  • Maintain a repository of data in order to track evidence and leverage previously collected and produced data
  • Serve as a primary point of contact with internal merits counsel, case teams, vendors and outside counsel law firms in order to execute processes throughout the EDRM lifecycle of legal matters
  • Manage and update eDiscovery data processing and production specifications for the Company
  • Consult with case teams to develop and implement eDiscovery technical project plans
  • Monitor and research emerging eDiscovery technology tools. Make recommendations on process improvements tied to new technology
  • Identify areas for overall process improvements and automation
  • Working knowledge of data mining tools to search, sort, and organize large amounts of electronic information
  • Train case teams on tools and technology to better support the life-cycle of legal matters
  • Maintain appropriate documentation (SOPs) including Chain of Custody and due diligence related to collections and processing

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree and five (5+) years experience with collection and processing technology, within a corporate legal environment or eDiscovery Service Provider
  • Proficient with eDiscovery platforms such as Nuix, M365, Relativity, SAAS Collection tools, and/or Proofpoint
  • Proficient with device collections, including experience with tools such as Cellebrite Digital Collector, Physical Analyzer and/or other similar products for imaging and extracting mobile device data; Paladin, EnCase, FTK and/or other similar products for forensic collection of physical devices
  • Ability to operate MacOS, Linux based OS, and/or similar Command Line Interface applications
  • Understanding of the Electronic Discovery Reference Model (EDRM)
  • Experience collecting and analyzing unstructured and structured datasets from various platforms
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, across cross-functional technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Work extended hours when necessary to ensure deadlines are met

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience providing testimony in support of eDiscovery collections and processes
  • Experience with scripting and database languages tools: Javascript, REST APIs, Python, PHP, Perl, SQL
  • eDiscovery and/or digital forensics certifications (including but not limited to EnCase, FTK, Nuix, Relativity, Cellebrite)

About the Team

Anduril develops advanced robotic systems that operate at the edge across land, sea, and air. Our team builds the critical systems powering everything from Group 1–3 autonomous aerial systems (such as Ghost, Anvil, Bolt, and Altius) to autonomous Sentry Towers that safeguard borders and critical infrastructure with real-time sensor fusion.
Underpinning these diverse robotic fleets is our DeviceOS team, which engineers the unified, highly reliable operating system and hardware-enablement platform that powers all of Anduril's autonomous assets. We take systems from initial schematics and paper sketches to hardened, field-ready robotics deployed in the most challenging operational environments on Earth.

About the Job

Underneath our airframes and Sentry Towers are custom carrier boards, embedded ARM architectures, and NVIDIA Jetson modules integrated with an intense array of hardware: electro-optical/infrared cameras, radars, CAN-connected sensor nodes, GPS, flight controllers, radios, and high-power motor drivers.
Between the silicon vendor’s raw Board Support Package (BSP) and our autonomous mission software sits a layer that must be owned deliberately: the boot chain, device trees, kernel drivers, and the guarantee that every piece of hardware deterministically enumerates and operates when our image boots.
In this role, you will own the boundary where custom hardware meets software. You will customize vendor BSPs and evaluate upstream changes. You will debug boot end-to-end—from firmware (EDK2/U-Boot) through unified kernel images to an encrypted root filesystem running at the tactical edge. You are the engineer who can read a schematic to diagnose a bus fault, remediate a kernel CVE on deployed hardware, and write the platform drivers that keep our robots flying and monitoring.
In this role, you will maintain and support a large deployed fleet by writing fixes for existing hardware and boot chains. This work is critical to our operations: a firmware regression is not just a failing test, it is a physical unit someone has to service in the field.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the Boot Path: Own the boot sequence end-to-end on deployed compute: low-level firmware, U-Boot/UEFI, unified kernel images, initrd, encrypted storage unlock, and handoff to a running NixOS environment. Debug boot failures on hardware via remote support.
  • Customize & Sustain Vendor BSPs: Reconcile vendor BSPs (Tegra/Jetson Linux, NXP, etc.) with modern NixOS package sets. Produce kernel and device tree patches when hardware requires custom behavior, and forward-port these changes across OS baseline upgrades.
  • Guarantee Deterministic Hardware Availability: Ensure all peripherals—cameras, radars, motor controllers, CAN networks, and radios—are reliably enumerated, correctly named, and fully operational across boots and platform upgrades.
  • Sustain a Long-Lived Baseline: Keep the existing signed boot chain and disk encryption working as the firmware, kernels, and package sets change underneath them. Triage and remediate CVEs in vendor kernels and low-level system components on our systems already deployed in the field.
  • Automate & Validate: Build and maintain automated Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test suites to catch regressions in power states, bus communication, and platform stability before code hits flight or field hardware.
  • Perform Deep Hardware/Software Root-Cause Analysis: Diagnose intermittent bus errors, thermal and power throttling issues, kernel panics, and boot hangs using serial consoles, logic analyzers, dmesg, and hardware schematics.
  • Be the Upstream: Triage upstream kernel and vendor BSP issues, produce the patch when no upstream fix is coming, and carry that patch set forward as the platform moves.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of professional embedded Linux platform, sustainment of deployed embedded Linux platforms, or kernel-adjacent integration experience.
  • Deep understanding of the embedded Linux boot chain: firmware/bootloaders (U-Boot, EDK2), device trees, kernel command line, initrd/initramfs, and root filesystem assembly.
  • Strong programming skills in C (for kernel/driver development and BSP patching) along with proficiency in Rust or C++ for userspace platform integration and services.
  • Hands-on experience debugging hardware at the bench: using serial consoles, reading schematics and component datasheets, and tracing issues to the board level.
  • Experience maintaining software deployed on real-world hardware, where updates must be safe, resilient to bricking, and strictly validated against regressions.
  • U.S. Person status is required due to export control regulations (ITAR/EAR), with eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Nix / NixOS Experience: Direct experience with declarative systems (Nix/NixOS) for embedded builds; or deep expertise in Yocto/Buildroot paired with an appetite to transition to modern, reproducible paradigms.
  • NVIDIA Jetson / Tegra Depth: Hands-on experience with JetPack, Jetson Linux BSP, Tegra boot architecture, or CUDA compute runtime integration.
  • Low-Level Platform Security: Practical implementation of hardware root-of-trust, secure boot, HAB/AHAB, or measured boot (TPM).
  • Automated HIL Testing: Experience architecting automated test benches using Python or Bash to validate embedded Linux builds against physical test targets.
  • Familiarity with functional programming paradigms (e.g., Nix, Haskell).
  • Upstream open-source contributions to the Linux kernel, U-Boot, or system-level open-source projects.

We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

  • No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

  • Please always verify communications:
    • Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com. 

  • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Enterprise Test Capabilities (ETC) develops, operates, and scales the shared physical test infrastructure, technical expertise, and execution systems required to validate Anduril's products across the company. The team provides specialized testing that is capital-intensive, technically complex, safety-critical, or broadly reusable across multiple programs, spanning environmental testing (thermal, vibration, shock, HALT, TVAC), battery testing (cell/module/pack characterization, abuse testing, BMS validation), propulsion testing (engine test cells, thrust/torque measurement, fuel/feed systems), aerodynamic testing (wind tunnel operations, flow visualization, force/moment measurement), and structural testing. We partner with product test teams from early development through qualification and sustainment to identify technical risk, select appropriate test methods, execute testing safely, and generate trusted engineering evidence. The test operations team within ETC owns the lab facilities, equipment fleet, calibration program, and operational support team that keeps this diverse test enterprise running.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking an Environmental Test Technician to join our rapidly growing environmental test team in Costa Mesa, CA. In this role, you will be responsible for executing a wide variety of climactic and environmental tests on the full spectrum of products developed at Anduril. The ideal candidate brings hands-on test and measurement equipment experience, strong troubleshooting instincts across multiple equipment types, and takes genuine pride in equipment performance and uptime. 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Execute a variety of environmental tests including, but not limited to, thermal, dynamic, corrosion, and ingress tests.
  • Program test controllers such as WATLOW F4s, and F4Ts.
  • Execute dynamic tests using electrodynamic shaker table control software.
  • Set up data acquisition systems for environmental tests
  • Maintain lab spaces to a high level of organization and professionalism.
  • Promote lab safety training and processes, fostering an environment and culture to promote safety as the number one priority
  • Promote proper maintenance of capital equipment including environmental chambers, electrodynamic shakers, and data acquisition equipment.
  • Advance environmental testing training materials and keep technical documentation updated.
  • Travel to test sites and remote labs as needed

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7+ years of professional experience in a engineering technician capacity or similar
  • Familiarity with Jira or other agile development software
  • Experience with running environmental test equipment
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, demanding, flexible team environment
  • Eligible to obtain / maintain a U.S. Security Clearance
  • Familiarity with environmental test standards (MIL-STD-810, DO-160)
  • 1st shift hours 6:00 AM - 2:30 PM

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Familiarity with NI Data acquisition system setup and collection, as well as running LabVIEW and Flexlogger software.
  • Familiarity with VR software including VibrationVIEW and ObserVIEW for executing and processing dynamic tests.
  • Demonstrated sense of drive and ability to work in cross-functional teams effectively

Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance. We are scaling at an historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base.

Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea—and this is the moment to join us.

ABOUT THE JOB

You will own payload integration within Mission Systems for a maritime autonomous vehicle, owning integration of Anduril and third-party payloads from concept through deployment. Reporting to the Mission Systems Lead, you will own payload interfaces, interoperability, mission development, and reference mission kits. You will ensure payloads meet customer mission requirements and integrate with the vehicle platform and autonomy stack.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own payload architecture: mechanical, electrical, and software interfaces for all mission payloads
  • Drive integration of Anduril payloads and government-furnished equipment onto the platform
  • Drive interoperability standards for payload modularity across vehicle configurations
  • Develop reference mission kits that package payloads with autonomy behaviors for specific mission sets
  • Define payload interface requirements and work with Vehicle Systems on accommodation
  • Manage payload integration schedule and cost across prototype and production phases
  • Coordinate with third-party vendors on payload qualification and integration
  • Provide technical mentorship to engineers across payload disciplines
  • Support testing and field deployment of payload systems
  • Represent the payload subsystem in technical and customer meetings
  • Interface with Mission Systems Lead and autonomy team on mission system integration
  • Travel up to 25% to test sites, vendor facilities, and customer locations

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent
  • 5+ years of experience in payload integration, weapons systems, or mission systems
  • Experience delivering payload integration in defense or aerospace environments
  • Demonstrated experience with sensor integration, weapons systems, or C4ISR payloads
  • Experience with the full product delivery lifecycle: design, test, manufacturing, deployment
  • Deep understanding of military mission sets and payload capabilities
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with maritime or undersea payload systems
  • Working knowledge of payload certification and weapons safety (MIL-STD-882E)
  • Experience with autonomous systems payload integration
  • Familiarity with modular open systems architecture (MOSA)
  • Prior Navy or defense operational experience

The Production Control team is responsible for a wide range of activities that are crucial to the manufacturing process including execution of the monthly production plan, coordinating the implementation of engineering changes, maintaining accurate inventory and government property, monitoring the health of the ERP and WMS systems and developing/implementing material flow strategies/processes to support efficient movement of material.


ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Production Coordinator to join our rapidly growing Manufacturing team in Atlanta, GA. In this role, you will be responsible for organizing and coordinating all aspects of production. Here you will work on cutting-edge technology aimed at advancing the state-of-the-possible. You will own resource planning, documentation, communicating with multiple stakeholders, problem solving and more! If you are a detail-oriented, self-starter interested in supporting production teams in a fast-paced environment, then this role is for you. 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Support the manufacturing/production, supply chain and inventory teams cross-functionally
  • Work with production managers to ensure all metrics driven action requirements are completed
  • Develop and maintain reports to highlight needs, deliverables and constraints as required for internal and customer use

  • 5+ years of experience in a manufacturing, shipping, or logistics environment
  • 3+ years of experience supporting administrative processes
  • Experience with MRP/ERP/MES (Netsuite, Oracle or equivalent systems)
  • Strong computer skills, familiar with the full suite of MS Office products
  • Tableau, Confluence, SQL or any reporting feature experience
  • Must be able to lift and move items of 20 pounds or more on a regular basis and repetitively lift weights on raised surfaces
  • Must be able to climb, bend, kneel, crawl, and stoop on a frequent basis and for extended periods
  • Willing to work overtime and weekends as needed
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

  • Experience in organizing files and documents
  • Inventory experience
  • Experience in aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, or electronic manufacturing environments
  • APICS certification
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Principles

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

Anduril develops advanced robotic systems that operate at the edge across land, sea, and air. Our team builds the critical systems powering everything from Group 1–3 autonomous aerial systems (such as Ghost, Anvil, Bolt, and Altius) to autonomous Sentry Towers that safeguard borders and critical infrastructure with real-time sensor fusion.
Underpinning these diverse robotic fleets is our DeviceOS team, which engineers the unified, highly reliable operating system and hardware-enablement platform that powers all of Anduril's autonomous assets. We take systems from initial schematics and paper sketches to hardened, field-ready robotics deployed in the most challenging operational environments on Earth.

About the Job

Underneath our airframes and Sentry Towers are custom carrier boards, embedded ARM architectures, and NVIDIA Jetson modules integrated with an intense array of hardware: electro-optical/infrared cameras, radars, CAN-connected sensor nodes, GPS, flight controllers, radios, and high-power motor drivers.
Between the silicon vendor’s raw Board Support Package (BSP) and our autonomous mission software sits a layer that must be owned deliberately: the boot chain, device trees, kernel drivers, and the guarantee that every piece of hardware deterministically enumerates and operates when our image boots.
In this role, you will own the boundary where custom hardware meets software. You will customize vendor BSPs and evaluate upstream changes. You will debug boot end-to-end—from firmware (EDK2/U-Boot) through unified kernel images to an encrypted root filesystem running at the tactical edge. You are the engineer who can read a schematic to diagnose a bus fault, remediate a kernel CVE on deployed hardware, and write the platform drivers that keep our robots flying and monitoring.
In this role, you will maintain and support a large deployed fleet by writing fixes for existing hardware and boot chains. This work is critical to our operations: a firmware regression is not just a failing test, it is a physical unit someone has to service in the field.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the Boot Path: Own the boot sequence end-to-end on deployed compute: low-level firmware, U-Boot/UEFI, unified kernel images, initrd, encrypted storage unlock, and handoff to a running NixOS environment. Debug boot failures on hardware via remote support.
  • Customize & Sustain Vendor BSPs: Reconcile vendor BSPs (Tegra/Jetson Linux, NXP, etc.) with modern NixOS package sets. Produce kernel and device tree patches when hardware requires custom behavior, and forward-port these changes across OS baseline upgrades.
  • Guarantee Deterministic Hardware Availability: Ensure all peripherals—cameras, radars, motor controllers, CAN networks, and radios—are reliably enumerated, correctly named, and fully operational across boots and platform upgrades.
  • Sustain a Long-Lived Baseline: Keep the existing signed boot chain and disk encryption working as the firmware, kernels, and package sets change underneath them. Triage and remediate CVEs in vendor kernels and low-level system components on our systems already deployed in the field.
  • Automate & Validate: Build and maintain automated Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test suites to catch regressions in power states, bus communication, and platform stability before code hits flight or field hardware.
  • Perform Deep Hardware/Software Root-Cause Analysis: Diagnose intermittent bus errors, thermal and power throttling issues, kernel panics, and boot hangs using serial consoles, logic analyzers, dmesg, and hardware schematics.
  • Be the Upstream: Triage upstream kernel and vendor BSP issues, produce the patch when no upstream fix is coming, and carry that patch set forward as the platform moves.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of professional embedded Linux platform, sustainment of deployed embedded Linux platforms, or kernel-adjacent integration experience.
  • Deep understanding of the embedded Linux boot chain: firmware/bootloaders (U-Boot, EDK2), device trees, kernel command line, initrd/initramfs, and root filesystem assembly.
  • Strong programming skills in C (for kernel/driver development and BSP patching) along with proficiency in Rust or C++ for userspace platform integration and services.
  • Hands-on experience debugging hardware at the bench: using serial consoles, reading schematics and component datasheets, and tracing issues to the board level.
  • Experience maintaining software deployed on real-world hardware, where updates must be safe, resilient to bricking, and strictly validated against regressions.
  • U.S. Person status is required due to export control regulations (ITAR/EAR), with eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Nix / NixOS Experience: Direct experience with declarative systems (Nix/NixOS) for embedded builds; or deep expertise in Yocto/Buildroot paired with an appetite to transition to modern, reproducible paradigms.
  • NVIDIA Jetson / Tegra Depth: Hands-on experience with JetPack, Jetson Linux BSP, Tegra boot architecture, or CUDA compute runtime integration.
  • Low-Level Platform Security: Practical implementation of hardware root-of-trust, secure boot, HAB/AHAB, or measured boot (TPM).
  • Automated HIL Testing: Experience architecting automated test benches using Python or Bash to validate embedded Linux builds against physical test targets.
  • Familiarity with functional programming paradigms (e.g., Nix, Haskell).
  • Upstream open-source contributions to the Linux kernel, U-Boot, or system-level open-source projects.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Anduril’s Manufacturing Safety Engineering team partners across Anduril’s manufacturing, engineering, and operations organizations to ensure our production systems are safe to build, test, and sustain at scale. As an engineering discipline, we design safety into the way products are made, covering the equipment, fixtures, test stations, and work instructions on the factory floor, rather than inspecting for it after the fact. Our mandate spans the production lifecycle, from new equipment and line design through ramp and sustained operations. We apply formal risk assessment and the hierarchy of controls to identify hazards early and engineer them out, partnering closely with our Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) experts, controls and manufacturing engineers, and production leadership to keep our people safe while moving at the speed Anduril demands.

ABOUT THE JOB
We are seeking experienced Manufacturing Safety Engineers to join our rapidly growing team in Quincy and engineer safety into how Anduril builds its products. As a Manufacturing Safety Engineer, you will apply formal risk assessment and the hierarchy of controls to production equipment, lift fixtures, test stations, and manufacturing work instructions, identifying hazards early and designing them out in partnership with EHS, manufacturing and controls engineering, and production teams. You will be the on-the-floor technical authority who makes our factories safe without slowing them down, from new equipment and line bring-up through ramp and sustained operations.
This is an evergreen requisition used to build a pipeline of Manufacturing Safety Engineers. This role is based in Costa Mesa, CA, and supports Anduril’s manufacturing operations, including sites at Quonset Point, RI and Atlanta, GA; specific team, site, and program assignments are determined during the interview process based on business need and candidate background.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Lead formal machine and task-based risk assessments on production equipment, fixtures, tooling, and processes, documenting hazards, risk ratings, required controls, and residual risk.
  • Review manufacturing work instructions and supporting training material for safety adequacy; author Job Hazard Analyses (JHA) and embed the required controls, PPE, and safe-work steps.
  • Engineer and review production equipment such as lift fixtures and material-handling aids in partnership with EHS, and support proof-load testing.
  • Assess and design safety into production test equipment.
  • Apply the hierarchy of controls and prevention-through-design principles to eliminate or reduce hazards at the equipment and line-design stage.
  • Define functional-safety requirements for safety-related control systems and verify their implementation.
  • Partner with EHS to ensure engineering controls satisfy applicable OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general-industry requirements (machine guarding, lockout/tagout, electrical, PPE, materials handling).
  • Support incident and near-miss investigations and root-cause analysis; drive corrective engineering actions and management of change.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • B.S. Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Industrial, or Safety Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline
  • 7+ years of experience in manufacturing/machine safety, equipment or controls engineering, or a related discipline with demonstrated ownership of risk assessments
  • Hands-on experience performing formal machine and task-based risk assessments and applying the hierarchy of controls
  • Working knowledge of machine safeguarding and applicable OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general-industry requirements, including machine guarding and the control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
  • Experience developing Job Hazard Analyses (JHA) and translating risk-assessment findings into work instructions, controls, and training
  • Experience designing safety into production and/or test equipment, partnering with EHS and electrical safety specialists
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence cross-functionally on the factory floor and with engineering teams
  • Eligibility to pursue and maintain a U.S. security clearance, as required

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Familiarity with machine safety standards such as ISO 12100 (risk assessment and risk reduction), ISO 13849 (safety-related parts of control systems), and ANSI B11 (machine safety and safeguarding)
  • M.S. Degree in an engineering discipline, or a professional safety credential (CSP, ASP) or machinery-safety credential (CMSE)
  • Functional-safety experience determining Performance Level or SIL for safety-related control systems, and functional-safety certification (CMSE or TÜV FSEng)
  • Experience with production test-equipment safety
  • Experience in a high-rate or rapidly scaling manufacturing environment, ideally in aerospace, defense, automotive, or a comparable regulated industry
  • Active U.S. security clearance
